meta.title: European integration
meta.question: Should Poland seek closer European integration or guard its independence?
meta.measure: Average position on European integration, from 0 (guard national independence) to 10 (closer integration)
meta.anchor: Pooled from questions on whether European unification should go further, on Poland's policy towards the EU and on adopting the euro, with every answer placed on 0 to 10 and the trend read on the scale of an average question.

items.wording: In general, to what extent are you for or against the unification of Europe, leading to the formation of a 'United States of Europe', including Poland? (for very much ... against very much)
items.notes: Central and Eastern Eurobarometer 1 (autumn 1990), 1 survey. V282 is a different question in later waves; their labels fail the check.

items.wording: Would you agree to replacing the złoty with the euro?
Foreign policy: closest possible cooperation with the EU (0) vs above all defend Poland's independence (10)
Should decisions on currency be taken solely by the Polish government or jointly within the European Union?
items.notes: Candidate Countries Eurobarometer 2000-03, 7 surveys. One area of the national-or-EU decision battery (24 areas); the others are left out (see notes).

items.wording: Own position: Poland should join the EU as soon as possible (0) vs protect our sovereignty (10)
items.notes: PGSW 2000 presidential study (SINGLE), 1 survey; the same 0-10 battery as PGSW_EU_POLICY_010.

items.wording: Should the European Union have a constitution?
items.notes: Candidate Countries Eurobarometer 2002-03, 3 surveys.

items.wording: Are you for or against Poland adopting the European currency, the euro? (very much against ... very much for; spontaneous 'neither' at 5)
items.notes: Candidate Countries Eurobarometer 2002-03, 3 surveys.

items.wording: European unification: gone too far (1) vs should be pushed further (10)
items.notes: European Election Study 2004, 1 survey (Poland used a 1-10 scale; only Sweden used 0-10).

items.wording: Are you for or against a constitution for the European Union?
items.notes: Standard Eurobarometer, autumn 2004 to spring 2007, 6 surveys: the Constitutional Treaty, a step of deepening.

items.wording: Are you for or against a European economic and monetary union with one single currency, the euro?
items.notes: Standard Eurobarometer, 2004-26, 45 surveys (EB 62.0 to 105.2). In a non-euro country this is support for the euro as EU policy, not specifically for Poland adopting it.

items.wording: The 'Euro-dynamometer': which speed of building Europe would you like, from 1 (at a standstill) to 7 (running as fast as possible)?
items.notes: Standard Eurobarometer, 2004-19, 11 surveys under four labels (PREFERENCE, DESIRED, UNFICATION [sic] SPEED - DESIRED, PREFERRED). The '(SUM)' recodes are excluded by the $ anchor. The 'current speed' twin (a perception) is not used.

items.wording: European unification has already gone too far (0) vs should go further (10)
items.notes: European Social Survey 2004-23.

items.wording: Are you personally happy or not that the euro could replace the złoty? (very happy ... very unhappy)
items.notes: Flash Eurobarometer, Mar 2006 to May 2011, 10 surveys: the support question before the 'in favour or against' wording replaced it.

items.wording: When would you like the euro to become your currency: as soon as possible, after a certain time, or as late as possible?
items.notes: Flash Eurobarometer, Mar 2006 to Apr 2015, 15 surveys (three answers; asked of everyone). The question number in the regex keeps out the 2016-26 version, whose fourth answer ('never') the 1-3 scale would drop. Bridges the change from FLASH_EURO_HAPPY to FLASH_EURO_FAVOUR.

items.wording: Poland should seek the closest possible integration within the EU vs keep as much independence as possible
items.notes: CBOS's two-statement self-placement cards, 2007-15.

items.wording: Which is closer to your view: the building of Europe must be pursued, or it has gone too far and we need to back-track? (neither at 5)
items.notes: Standard Eurobarometer 70.1 (autumn 2008), 1 survey.

items.wording: Some say European unification should be pushed further, others that it has already gone too far: where would you place yourself? (0 gone too far, 10 pushed further)
items.notes: European Election Study 2009 and 2019 (0-10 codes), 2 surveys. The same question in 2004 (codes 1-10) and 2014 (codes 1-11) is in the next two items: their label checks keep each version to its own wave.

items.wording: Foreign policy: closest possible cooperation (0) vs defend our sovereignty above all (10)
items.notes: CBOS's two-statement self-placement cards, 2010.

items.wording: Foreign policy towards the EU, as above, 1-7
European unification, as above, 1-7
items.notes: PGSW 2011.

items.wording: Generally speaking, are you personally more in favour or against the idea of introducing the euro in Poland? (very much in favour ... very much against)
items.notes: Flash Eurobarometer on the euro in non-euro member states, Nov 2011 to Apr 2026, 16 yearly surveys (telephone, later online), about 1,000 Poles each.

items.wording: The EU should develop further into a federation of nation states (agree-disagree)
items.notes: Standard Eurobarometer, Nov 2012 to May-June 2014, 4 surveys.

items.wording: To deal with Europe's economic problems, would you favour or oppose giving more decision-making power to the EU?
items.notes: Pew Global Attitudes spring 2013 and 2014, 2 surveys.

items.wording: More decisions should be taken at EU level (agree-disagree)
items.notes: Standard Eurobarometer, 2014-26, 25 surveys (EB 81.2 to 105.2).

items.wording: European unification: gone too far (0) vs should be pushed further (10), coded 1-11 in the file
items.notes: European Election Study 2014, 1 survey.

items.wording: Poland should adopt the euro as soon as possible vs never
items.notes: CBOS's two-statement self-placement cards, 2015.

items.wording: European unification has already gone too far (0) vs Europe should unite even more (10)
When would you like the euro to become your currency: as soon as possible, after a certain time, as late as possible, or never?
items.notes: Flash Eurobarometer, Apr 2016 to Apr 2026, 11 surveys (four answers, 'never' added).

items.wording: Future of the EU: national governments should transfer more powers to the EU / the current division should remain / some powers should be returned to national governments
items.notes: Pew Global Attitudes spring 2016, 1 survey. Middle option at 5.

items.wording: Poland should act to reduce EU control over changes in Polish law (agree-disagree)
items.notes: POLPAN 2018, 1 wave. Its twin on reducing EU influence on traditions and national culture (TE06B) is left out as closer to nationalism.

items.wording: What is your view on European unification? 0 = it has already gone too far, 10 = Europe should unite even more
items.notes: SWPS COVID tracker, waves 1-13 and 15 (March 2020 to November 2021), 14 surveys; online quota samples. Wave 12 labels a non-existent code 11 as '10'; unused.

items.wording: After the epidemic, member states should transfer more competences to the EU level (agree-disagree)
items.notes: SWPS COVID tracker wave 5 (May 2020), 1 survey; online. The middle code is 'hard to say' and is left out (no position).

items.wording: European unification has already gone too far (0) vs should go further (10)
items.notes: ESS round 10 (2021-22): self-completion by web and paper in Poland, where every other round was face to face, so a question of its own.

items.wording: European unification has already gone too far (0) vs should be pushed further (10)
items.notes: European Election Study 2024 (by name), 1 survey; online.

items.wording: A: to solve common problems states should hand more powers to international organisations, even at the cost of national control, vs B: each nation should decide its own policy (1 full support for A ... 7 full support for B)
items.notes: Postliberalism survey 2025 (SINGLE), 1 survey. International organisations in general, not the EU by name: include only if the trend is meant as sovereignty versus pooling.
